faq.q: What is the minimum age to rent a yacht in Marbella in 2030?
faq.a: The marbella yacht charter minimum age policy 2030 states you must be at least 18 years old to book a skippered charter. For bareboat (self-drive) charters, the minimum age is 25–30 depending on the boat size and your licence. All our listed boats come with a licensed skipper, so passengers of any age can join.

faq.q: Can I charter a yacht in Marbella if I am under 21?
faq.a: Yes, if you are 18–20 you can book a skippered charter for a family or private group. However, for party or youth-oriented groups, we require the lead booker to be at least 21. This is to ensure responsible behaviour. Contact us on WhatsApp for specific cases.

faq.q: Is there a minimum age for children on a yacht charter?
faq.a: No minimum age for children — infants are welcome on all our skippered charters. We provide life jackets for children under 12 free of charge. The Mangusta 80 (24m) and Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) are particularly family-friendly with shaded decks and cabins.

faq.q: What ID do I need to prove my age for a yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: A valid passport or EU national ID card is required for all lead bookers. We check age at check-in at Puerto Banús. If you look under 25, we may ask for ID even if you are over 18. Digital copies on your phone are accepted.

faq.q: Can a group of 18-year-olds charter a yacht in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, but only with a licensed skipper. Our marbella yacht charter minimum age policy 2030 requires the lead booker to be 18+ for private, non-party charters. For larger party groups, the minimum rises to 21. The Astondoa 40 (9 pax) or Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) are popular choices.

faq.q: Do I need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella?
faq.a: If you book a skippered charter (all our boats), no licence is needed — our skipper handles everything. For bareboat charters, you need a valid International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or equivalent, plus proof of experience. Minimum age for bareboat is 25.

faq.q: What happens if someone in my group is under 18?
faq.a: Nothing — under-18s are welcome as passengers. The marbella yacht charter minimum age policy 2030 only applies to the person making the booking. We do require a parent or guardian to sign a waiver for any minor under 18. The Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) and Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are great for small families.

faq.q: Are there age restrictions for jet skis or water toys?
faq.a: Jet skis (included free on Mangusta 80 charters) require the driver to be 18+ with a valid licence or a brief safety briefing. Passengers of any age can ride. Towable tubes and inflatables have no age limit but must follow the skipper's safety instructions. Life jackets are mandatory for all ages on water toys.

Planning a yacht charter in Marbella for 2030? The marbella yacht charter minimum age policy 2030 is straightforward: you must be 18 to book a skippered charter, and there is no minimum age for passengers. All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, and every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% IVA. Whether you are planning a family day out or a birthday cruise, here is exactly what the age rules mean for you.

Minimum Age to Rent a Yacht in Marbella (2030 Update)

The legal minimum age to enter into a charter contract in Spain is 18 years old. This applies to all skippered charters in our fleet — from the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) at €749/2h to the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). If you are under 18, a parent or legal guardian must book on your behalf. No exceptions. For bareboat charters (not offered by us), Spanish regulations require a minimum age of 25 and a valid ICC (International Certificate of Competence).

Age Rules for Party & Youth Groups

If your group plans to cruise along the Golden Mile or anchor at Caleta del Faro, and the vibe is more party than picnic, the lead booker must be 21 or older. This is part of the marbella yacht charter minimum age policy 2030 to ensure responsible behaviour on the water. Groups of 18–20 year olds can still charter, but only for private, non-party trips. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719/4h (includes a free jet ski) is a favourite for celebrations — but the booker must meet the age requirement.

Children & Infants: No Minimum Age

Families are welcome aboard. There is no minimum age for children or infants on any of our skippered charters. We provide life jackets for children under 12 free of charge. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) and Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax) are popular with families thanks to their stable platforms and shaded areas. Children must be supervised by an adult at all times, and the skipper has final say on safety. For a small family, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are affordable options.

ID Requirements at Check-In

All lead bookers must present a valid passport or EU national ID card at check-in in Puerto Banús. If you look under 25, we may request ID even if you are over 18. Digital copies on your phone are accepted. For groups with minors, a parent or guardian must sign a waiver. No ID? No charter — no refunds. This is standard across all Marbella marinas, including Marbella Marina and Cabopino.

Bareboat vs. Skippered: Age & Licence Differences

All our boats come with a licensed skipper — so you never need a licence. The marbella yacht charter minimum age policy 2030 for skippered charters is simply 18 to book. If you want to captain the boat yourself (bareboat), you would need to be 25–30 years old with an ICC and proof of experience. We do not offer bareboat charters, but if you have a licence and want to self-drive, we can point you to partners. For 99% of clients, a skippered charter is safer, easier, and more relaxing.
